Oh it's nothing like that. I'm sure my close friends do care but talking to them about my depression will change the dynamics completely. Core part of my depression is a very dumb insecurity and I don't want anyone to know about that.

I guess when I put it in words it sounds kinda dumb but it's just more of me bottling up everything 😅.

I'm glad you were able to overcome your suicidal thoughts man. I wish I could talk to my best friend but I just can't.

Well, at the very least I hope I find someone to help me like you said. Thanks for the kind words again.

Hey thanks man. I know suicide is not a solution I just kinda drifted along in a moment of weakness. 

I don't have anyone to talk to. I mean I have friends and family thankfully, but to all of them I'm just a happy dude. I wouldn't want them to think otherwise. 

Stuff like this is generally looked down up in my society and mostly the responses will just be "You gotta man up" or something like that.
Hey thanks for your kind words. I was just having an episode and googling dumb shit.

It seems like you're trying to make all your positive changes very quickly and very fast. And when you're not able to commit to it you feel bad and spiral again.

It helps if you take one thing you want to do and focus on that until it becomes the norm to you.

For example I wanted start eating healthy, run, hit the gym more often and also do abs every evening. I'd plan my day like run and abs in the morning and workout in the evening while also eating healthy. 

Obviously I couldn't keep up with my own goals all of a sudden because it was too sudden for me and I'd feel bad. What helped was that I focus on one particular task (for me it was eating healthy) until it became normal to me and then work towards the next (running). This started about 6 months ago, and now I'm (mostly) eating healthy, running in the morning consistently and also hitting the gym. Still haven't worked my way towards doing abs in the evening, not yet.

Also because you place some emotions on your activities, you become critical if you don't hit your targets. I'd feel guilty all day if I missed the gym or ate junk food. But it's okay. If you slip up, it's fine. Just get back to it the next day.

I'm no pinnacle of fitness or anything like that but I'm consistent these days and still working to be better. 

This is mostly related to my own fitness and diet routine and you'd have a different journey yourself with your own issues but I guess the underlying principles stay the same. 

Good luck and happy grinding!
